claims.statement: Interactive capability cannot live in the wallpaper layer: a Wallpaper Engine desktop web wallpaper receives neither clicks nor keyboard focus, which is why desktop arrangement uses Win32 icon messages and why the search panel is a service-owned window, with both ADRs rejecting an extra resident process on the same grounds.

AGENT DECK is a single-machine Windows Electron application whose production topology is three processes plus a guard: an outer supervisor started by plain `electron .`, a panel main process spawned as a `--panel` child that owns the window, hotzone input, bridge and plugin host, and a utilityProcess child (service name deck-dataplane) that owns all periodic collection; a detached icon-restore-watch.cjs guard is the only additional process. ADR-0004 fixes the Electron host plus cordis kernel and ADR-0005 fixes this process split.

The outer supervisor performs the machine-level duties around the panel: it takes the single-instance lock but releases it before spawning the panel child (so a still-shutting-down previous instance cannot be mistaken for a second launch), hides explorer's native desktop icons before the panel is raised, spawns the detached restore guard only when it actually hid them, and restores the icons when the panel child exits.

Single-instance and recall are split across the two processes: a second `electron .` launch is refused in milliseconds by the supervisor's lock (with a `single-instance-refused` evidence line), while the panel process holds its own lock so a `second-instance` event recalls the existing panel by showing it without focus and re-pinning it to the bottom.

Panel boot has a fixed ordering: start the kernel, wait for the data plane's first snapshot before creating the window, then install the plugin protocol and wire bridge and window-host IPC; a 15-second ready timeout releases the wait so the panel starts with empty data sections that the next snapshot fills instead of not starting at all.

The two structural red lines of ADR-0005 hold in code: click-through is `setIgnoreMouseEvents(true)` without Electron's `forward` option (forwarding installs a global WH_MOUSE_LL hook on the window-host thread), with hotzone hit testing done by a 25 ms main-process cursor poll plus a two-poll leave confirmation and a 500 ms re-pin throttle; and collection never runs on the panel main event loop, because the production assembly registers no collection service and the four collectors live in the child.

The main process and the data-plane child speak one structured-clone message protocol (init, ready, snapshot, resolve-shortcuts, shortcuts, req, res); the main process caches the newest snapshot and answers every bridge read from that cache, and only `desktop/move` and `desktop/reset-layout` can be sent to the child as requests.

A data-plane child exit rejects pending RPCs and restarts the child with 1 s to 30 s exponential backoff; placement, the usage log and session/desktop scans converge from disk after the restart, and only the hardware history rings restart empty, which is accepted as a display-only loss.

Because Electron APIs are unavailable to the data-plane child, the main process resolves and ships the desktop roots, placement store path, usage directory and docMaxRows in the init message, answers batched lnk target-resolution RPCs from the child, preheats icons with `app.getFileIcon` from snapshot items, and validates `desktop/launch` against its own snapshot item pool before calling `shell.openPath`.

Capabilities are cordis Service plugins assembled in code by three functions: `createKernel` (all services in-process, used by the offline kernel tests), `createDataplaneKernel` (the four collection services, used by the child entry) and `createPanelKernel` (the Electron production main process); the bridge reaches data sections only through the `PanelDataPort` seam, implemented by `LocalPanelDataService` in-process and by `DataplaneService` in production.

`app/src/shared/contract.ts` is the only kernel-to-renderer API shape (PanelSnapshot sections, BridgeMethods, BridgeEvents) and is meant to be extended rather than forked into new channels; it travels over `deck:bridge-invoke` with an ok/error envelope and over `deck:bridge-event`, while hotzone declarations, keyboard mode and evidence notify use a separate window-host channel in the same `window.deck` namespace, and the renderer runs sandboxed with contextIsolation on and node integration off.

Session state comes from five external AI tool stores read through one strictly read-only seam, `collectSessions(roots, now)`, whose per-tool scanners open SQLite with `readOnly: true` and a 500 ms busy timeout; a failing tool is skipped with a warning while the remaining tools still report.

The cold-start usage prior is read from the UserAssist registry key by exporting it with `reg.exe export` into a temp file and parsing the UTF-16LE text; the read is asynchronous so it cannot block boot, and any failure yields an empty prior rather than a startup problem.

Only the panel main process talks to Listary's loopback API (POST /api/v1/search on 127.0.0.1 at config.search.port, default 38431, with a new connection per request and a 3 s timeout) and search queries are stored nowhere; an unreachable engine surfaces as the engine-offline state with a 3 s retry that affects only the search overlay.

Hiding and restoring explorer's native desktop icons is the only external OS state the application toggles, done with one `WM_COMMAND 0x7402` message to SHELLDLL_DefView; the icon list view's visibility is treated as the fact and the HideIcons registry value as the user's preference, so restore fires only when this run hid the icons and they are still hidden, and `--icon-restore` forces them visible without taking the single-instance lock.

The panel maintains its own Startup shortcut `AGENT DECK.lnk` through a PowerShell helper under a production-run gate: only a run whose app directory equals the declared `config.autostart.appDir` may create it or take over a dead chain, a live chain pointing elsewhere is never retargeted, the retired watchdog link `qoder-deck-server-watchdog.lnk` is deleted on every boot regardless of who is running, `enabled=false` removes the link, and an autostart failure never blocks the panel from starting.

`app/config.json` is the user-editable production configuration: it is written with defaults derived from the primary display on first boot, invalid fields fall back to their defaults with a warning rather than being swallowed, and `panel`, `weather` and `desktop` are read once at boot (a change needs a restart) while the appearance setting is rewritten to the file by the settings service and pushed live.

Runtime state lives in Electron's `userData` — `layout.json` for placement and `usage/` for the usage JSONL — never in the code directory, and the Python-era `%LOCALAPPDATA%\qoder-deck\usage\` log is copied into it once, idempotently, on first boot rather than moved.

The panel hosts desktop items itself: the item pool is built from the user and public desktop directories with hidden and system entries filtered out and same-name items resolved in favour of the user desktop, and placement is persisted as ordered name lists (pinned, dock, docs) instead of coordinates because the panel, not explorer, draws the items.

The panel window is created frameless, transparent and non-focusable and is pinned to HWND_BOTTOM with `SetWindowPos` (an FFI call, since Electron has no bottom-pinning level) on startup, on hotzone leave, on focus and after every recall; keyboard mode — used for the search overlay and the settings slider — is the single temporary exception that makes it focusable and then restores non-focusability and re-pins.

Desktop components are the extension boundary: a plugin directory holds a `plugin.json` manifest (id doubling as the `deck-plugin://` host name, name, version, an in-directory .js/.mjs entry, capabilities intersected with the snapshot section names, optional mount/order), assets are served by the privileged `deck-plugin://` scheme with reads in the main process and root containment enforced (404 otherwise), directory watching makes hot-plugging visible through `plugins/changed` without waiting for the next snapshot, and the built-in cards root is scanned first so a user plugin cannot displace a built-in id.

Failures degrade one section or duty and never the panel: a broken tool store, an unreachable Listary, an absent GPU, a malformed `plugin.json`, a desktop scan error (the previous item pool is kept), a failed icon hide (dual-desktop degradation is logged) and a failed autostart write are all reported and skipped without blocking the desktop from appearing.

The offline vitest suite covers the pure logic seams and the kernel/bridge contract seams with injected fakes, while the Electron-only paths — the utilityProcess glue, Win32 pointer and pinning behaviour, icon carry and the plugin asset protocol — are covered by the real-machine `--accept` battery, and `--icon-restore` is the one-shot self-rescue entry that runs without taking the single-instance lock.

The application is run from a checkout rather than installed: `app/package.json` declares only cordis and koffi as runtime dependencies (electron, typescript and vitest are dev dependencies), the build is `tsc` for main plus `tsc` for the renderer plus an asset copy with no bundler, and the renderer is native ESM reached through the `deck-plugin://` scheme.

The window geometry is generated from the primary display bounds and stored in `config.json`, but the renderer's card, document-zone and dock rectangles are fixed DIP constants that the acceptance battery asserts against, so the layout is tuned for the single production machine and porting it means editing those constants rather than the config.

The earlier form of this system is retired rather than coexisting: the Python data service (`server.py`), its autostart watchdog, the Tk search window, the Win32 real-desktop-icon arrangement chain and the three Wallpaper Engine deployment scripts went away on 2026-09-29, and the wallpaper assets are frozen read-only under `archive/`, referenced by no build, test or runtime path.
